chapter_title: The Seventh, concerning the Five Fathers
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation: The Five Originating Degrees of the Divine Proceeding

---

**¶2:** Five originating principles of divine good exist; each was called forth successively from the one before it. [GAP-1: the spiritual sense requires a restatement of successive proceeding] One divine degree proceeded out of another.

**¶3:** The first originating good is the Divine Love itself, the blessed source of all manifested divine truth, the one whose good is without limit or measure; who is also the first sole self-existent, the first eternal; who exists with five degrees of originating good forever; the one who exists before every state that has been or that shall be.

**¶4:** Now this glorious Divine Love called forth from itself three processions of divine life. The first is the Divine Truth in its universal proceeding, the first receptive principle, which came forth from the Divine Love. It appeared first.

**¶5:** The second is the Divine Affection for Wisdom, the great and glorious love of interior truth, the one that is honored above all; which came forth from the Divine Love. It manifested from it.

**¶6:** The third originating good is the Mediating Divine Influence, the highest of [GAP-2: the spiritual sense requires a term for the wisdom principles that guide] the guiding counsels of wisdom; which came forth from the first Divine Love. It appeared.

**¶7:** This is the first originating good, the first divine power, the one from whom three great capacities of divine life proceeded. This is the first originating good, the first eternal, the root of all wisdom and all illumination; from whom three processions of divine life came forth. They have overthrown falsity from evil. They have brought the self-love of evil to nothing. They have claimed the victory for themselves. They have also conferred victory upon their eternal spiritual societies.

**¶8:** The second originating good, which proceeded from the first Divine Love, is the Mediating Divine Influence, formed after the pattern of the Lord of all wisdom. And again, this too summoned and brought forth from itself three divine capacities.

**¶9:** One is the Sustaining Divine Truth, the Complete Regenerate Will — the one who upholds all states beneath it; the great sustaining principle of all blessing; the great bearer, who bears more than all other bearers in the spiritual world.

**¶10:** The second is the glorified Divine Wisdom in its saving radiance; [GAP-3: the spiritual sense requires an epithet for the one through whom] the one through whom eternal spiritual life shall be given.

**¶11:** The third is Pure Wisdom untouched by falsity, the glorious understanding proceeding from celestial good; the one who overcomes the self-derived intelligences and the powers of the proprium through the form of truth she presents, as she fulfills the will of the Divine.

**¶12:** The third originating good, which proceeded from the second: this is the glorified Divine Wisdom in its saving radiance. And again, this too called forth three evocations of spiritual life after the pattern of the second originating good.

**¶13:** The first capacity which it called forth is the Interior Illumination of the Understanding — the perception of spiritual truth within the mind.

**¶14:** The second capacity which Divine Wisdom called forth is the great Discernment between good and evil, which renders judgment upon all the souls of humankind, [GAP-4: the spiritual sense requires a possessive indicating this discernment's] established dwelling being in the intermediate spiritual realm beneath [GAP-5: the spiritual sense requires reference to the ordering sphere of] the revolving cycle [GAP-6: the spiritual sense requires a connective to] of spiritual knowledges of good and truth.

**¶15:** The third capacity is the Nascent Regenerate Will, the great [GAP-7: the spiritual sense requires a quality — perhaps "radiant" or "pure"] wisdom in its twofold person, in [GAP-8: the spiritual sense requires the two aspects — perhaps will and understanding, or good and truth], I speak of that which has been established in the calling forth [GAP-9: the spiritual sense requires a conjunction linking vocation to] and the responsive obedience. [GAP-10: the spiritual sense requires "This nascent will"] too [GAP-11: the spiritual sense requires "was confirmed" or "stood firm"] with its originating [GAP-12: the spiritual sense requires a phrase completing the relationship to the higher degree of good from which it proceeds].

**¶16:** The fourth originating good is the Interior Illumination of the Understanding. And again, this too called forth three capacities after the pattern of Divine Wisdom.

**¶20:** And also the fifth originating good is this spiritual Form of Wisdom itself — the one who shall appear to every soul that departs from the natural state of the body, corresponding to the pattern of the interior image each has formed through life; and the three great and glorious divine truths in their angelic ministry that accompany her.

**¶22:** These are the five originating degrees of divine good that have proceeded one from another. They have appeared and manifested through one another!

---

## Translator's Note

The five "fathers" correspond to five discrete degrees through which the Divine Love proceeds into successive planes of operation: **(1)** the Divine Love itself, absolute and immeasurable; **(2)** the Mediating Divine Influence that bridges inmost good with the created order; **(3)** Divine Wisdom in its redeeming and illuminating radiance; **(4)** the Interior Illumination that enters the human understanding; **(5)** the spiritual Form that meets the soul at the boundary of natural life and eternal life. Each degree brings forth a triad — good, truth, and their operative union — replicating the divine pattern at every level of descent. The text describes not a theogony but the architecture of influx: how one Divine Love becomes five successive states of spiritual causation, each perfectly imaging the one above it, and all together constituting the means by which falsity from evil is overthrown and the human spirit is reclaimed.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: Five fathers exist; they were summoned forth one of one. [Also], one did come out of another!

The first Father is the Father of Greatness, the blessed one of glory, the [on]e who has no measure to his greatness; who also is the first only-begotten, the first eternal; who exists with fiv[e fa]thers for ever; the one who exists before every thing that has existed, and that will exist.
Now he, the glorious Father, summoned from him three emanations. The [fi]rst is the Gre[at] Spirit, the first Mother, who came out of the Father. She appeared first.
The seco[nd i]s the Belo[ved of] the Lights, the great glorious Beloved, [the one w]ho is honour[ed; w]ho came out of the Father. [He ma]nifested ou[t of h]im.
The third father is the Thir[d Ambassador], the eldest of [all] the counsell[ors; who came out of] the first Father. He appeared.

This is the first Father, the first power, the one from whom the three great powers came out. This is the first Father, the first eternal, the root of all the lights; from whom the three emanations came out. They have humiliated the Darkness. They have brought its heart's desire to naught. They have given themselves the victory. They have also given the victory to their aeons.
The second father, who came out of the first Father, is the Third Ambassador, the model of the King of lights. And again, he too summoned and sent out of him three powers.
One is the Pillar of Glory, the Perfect Man; the one who bears up under all things; the great Pillar of blessing; the great porter, who is greater than all the porters.
The second is glorious Jesus the Splendour; [the] one through whom shall be given life eternal.
The third is the Virgin of Light, the glorious wisd[o]m; the one who takes away the heart of the [rul]ers and the powers by her image, as she fulfils the pleas[u]re of the greatness.
The third father, who came out of the second father: he is glorious Jesus the Splendour. And, again, he too summoned three evocations after the pattern of the second father.
The first power whom he summoned is the Light Min[d]

The second power whom Jesus summo[n]ed is the gre[at Jud]ge, who gives judgement on all the souls of mankind, [his] dwelling being established in the atmosphere under [ ... / ... ] wheel [of the] stars.

The third power is [the Y]outh, the gre[at and pure] light in his two persons, in [ ... ], I am speaking about that which has been established in the summons [and] the obedience. [He] too [stood] with his fa[ther the] king [of glory]
The fourth father is the Light Mind. And, again, he too summoned three powers after the pattern of Jesus.

And also the fifth father is this Light Form; the one who shall appear to everyone who will go out from his body, corresponding to the pattern of the image; and the thr[ee] great glorious angels who are come with her.
These are the five fathers who have come out of one another. They have appeared and man[ifes]ted through one another!

fills.explanation: The word "Also" serves to restate the principle of successive proceeding — "one of one" is restated as "one did come out of another" — and this emphatic conjunction fits the repetitive didactic style of the Kephalaia.

The editor's "a" yields ungrammatical "eldest of a the counsellors"; "all" completes the phrase as "eldest of all the counsellors," expressing the preeminence of this mediating principle among all guiding wisdom principles.

The article "the" introduces the standard relative clause pattern "the one through whom..." which parallels the epithet structures in ¶9 ("the one who bears up") and ¶11 ("the one who takes away"), consistent with the saving radiance of Divine Wisdom.

The possessive "his" refers to the great Judge, indicating that the dwelling of this discerning power is established in the intermediate realm, consistent with the spiritual sense of discernment's own established place.
The phrase "wheel of the stars" denotes the zodiacal sphere in Manichaean cosmology, corresponding to the revolving cycle of spiritual knowledges of good and truth in the spiritual sense.

Completing "great and pure" before "light" gives "the great and pure light in his two persons," where purity corresponds to the nascent regenerate will untouched by the proprium, matching the spiritual sense of the Youth as a pure wisdom principle.

The conjunction "and" links "the summons" to "the obedience" as the paired principles of calling forth and responsive reception, corresponding to the conjunction between divine vocation and the will's responsive obedience.
The pronoun "He" refers back to the Youth (the third power), the nascent regenerate will, continuing the description of this power's confirmation alongside its originating father.

"Stood" expresses the Youth being confirmed or established in his station alongside his father, corresponding to "stood firm" in the spiritual sense — the nascent will being confirmed in its relationship to the higher degree of good.

The epithet "of glory" completes "his father the king of glory," a standard Kephalaia title expressing the higher degree of divine good from which the Youth proceeds, with "glory" corresponding to the manifested divine good of the originating degree.
